chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Hilal al-Razi said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man appointed an agent to divorce his wife when she menstruates and becomes pure. The man went out, and it occurred to him (to change his mind), and he testified that he had annulled what he had ordered him to do, and that it had occurred to him regarding that. He (peace be upon him) said: Let him inform his family and let him inform the agent.
ai.seo_question: How does a man revoke a delegated divorce if he changes his mind after appointing the agent?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the revocability of delegated divorce (*tawkil*) under Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the principal retains the right to rescind the agent's authority prior to execution. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that validity requires notifying both the family (to prevent social confusion) and the agent (to prevent unilateral action), highlighting the procedural rigor of agency in marital contracts. This ruling underscores the flexibility of *talaq* as a revocable act until the condition is fully actualized by the agent.
